I'm also checking the renewal caption logic: hosting and email don't show a "Then $X" line, while VPS gates it on the plan. I need to compute renewalTotalCents correctly for hosting by subtracting 10% when a partner is attached, even though it's currently only surfaced in one caption spot, so I need to trace the recurring discount path before finalizing that.

For the wizard, I'm planning a new server-side quoteHostingOrder function that takes plan, term, and extra disk parameters, checks user auth and first-month-free eligibility via IP hash, and returns the computed totals matching the order path's logic.

Now I'm weighing whether to add a matching quoteEmailOrder in a separate file since each file should export one function, and considering whether to replace the instant matrix-lookup pricing for hosting/email in order.tsx with this async server quote instead — which would leave the catalog's hardcoded free-month cents unused but better matches the pattern already used for games. How Nxeon actually started

We didn’t set out to build a hosting company. One invoice changed that.

We’re three brothers, not a founding committee. We left ordinary jobs in Canada to go travel, ended up building a website together in Da Nang, Vietnam, and needed a server to put it on. We picked an ordinary host. The renewal bill taught us more about the hosting industry than anything since, and it’s the whole reason Nxeon exists.

Create your account→See pricing
Where it started

A rooftop, a website, and a server we needed by the end of the week

None of us had run a company before. We’d spent our 9-to-5s doing perfectly normal things back in Canada, saved up, and left to see more of the world than a two-week vacation allows. Da Nang is where we ended up staying longest, long enough that “get a server” stopped being a someday task and became something we actually had to do that week.

We were putting together a simple booking website for a friend’s small business back home, the kind of favour-turned-project that always takes longer than anyone expects. It needed somewhere to live, so we did what everyone does: signed up with the first host whose plan looked cheap enough, and got back to actually enjoying the trip.

Hosting renewalInvoice
The price we signed up for
The renewal

Same plan. Same server. No explanation beyond an email we’d almost skimmed past.

The turn

Then the renewal came due

The first term was fine, cheap even. Then the renewal notice landed, and the price on it had nothing to do with the price we’d signed up for. We read it twice, then a third time, assuming we’d missed something in the fine print. We hadn’t. It was just quietly, a lot more.

What actually got us wasn’t the money. It was realizing, once we started asking around, that this wasn’t one host having a bad quarter. It’s a pattern a lot of hosting companies lean on: quote a low price to get you in the door, then raise it at renewal once your DNS is pointed, your site is live, and switching feels like more hassle than it’s worth. We were exactly the naive first-time customers that trick is built for.

So we did the thing you do when something annoys you enough on a trip: we kept talking about it long after we should have dropped it. By the time we were back to working on our own projects full-time, “let’s just build the host we wished we’d had” had stopped being a joke.

What we built instead

Lock in your price today.

The price you sign up at is the price you renew at. It never increases at renewal.

That’s not a slogan a marketing team workshopped. There is no marketing team, there’s the three of us. It’s the direct fix for the exact problem that started this whole thing: sign up for a Cloud VPS, a game server, shared hosting, business email or a domain at Nxeon, and the number on your renewal invoice is the same number you saw on day one.

See how pricing works
What we actually built

Not a pitch deck’s idea of hosting

The five things we run today, for real customers, from that same instinct: build the thing we’d have wanted.

{{nxm:products:html}}
Who’s actually running this

Three brothers, three very different jobs

No departments, no org chart. Just three people who happen to be good at different parts of the same problem.

The one who won’t stop touching servers

Spends most days in Proxmox and firewall rules, obsessing over the boring parts, isolation, backups, uptime, that nobody notices until they’re missing.

The one who actually finishes things

Built the original travel-project website that started all this, and now builds the dashboard, the checkout, and yes, this page.

The one who replies to your ticket

Handles support, billing, and the part of running a company that’s just talking to people honestly when something goes wrong.

“Built with love in Vietnam” is true in the plain sense: that’s where Nxeon runs from, day to day. The servers themselves live in {{nxm:regions}}. Home base and hardware don’t have to be the same place. In our case, they aren’t.

If you’ve ever opened a renewal email and felt your stomach drop a little, we built this for you, mostly because we’ve been you. And if the price ever changes on you, tell us. That would mean we broke our own rule.

Deploy your first server in under a minute

Creating an account is free and takes no card details. You pay when you deploy: choose a billing term and pay from your wallet or by card at checkout.

I notice the VPS renewal display in "My Services" also doesn't account for the partner percentage, similar to another pre-existing gap I should flag in my report. Now I'm planning the implementation: I'll add a helper function to adjust base pricing for partners, likely placing it in the pricing library or a dedicated partner utility file.

For the actual logic, I'm designing a pure function that applies a partner discount to a base amount and returns the discount amount, net amount, and effective tier — making it testable in isolation, with the tier resolving to "NONE" when there's no chargeable amount (like a free hosting month) so no discount claim or line item gets shown incorrectly.

Then for hosting orders, I'm working through resolving the partner discount before charging, computing the anticipated net cents, and within the transaction applying the discount to the debited amount — capturing the discount cents and tier for the invoice, and updating the wallet transaction description to note the partner discount.

I'm also considering invoice line items showing the base price plus a negative partner discount line, and whether to add an inline commission accrual right after invoice creation for hosting orders — deciding this is safe since it's the same accrual logic just triggered earlier, with the nightly sweep as a backstop if invoice creation fails. I want to consolidate the discount-and-pricing logic into a shared hosting-pricing helper to avoid duplicating it across the order placement and external payment quoting paths.

I'm planning a similar shared helper for email pricing...

For email, the promo never applies but I need to keep applying the partner discount on the post-promo base within the transaction, mirroring hosting. Then I need to handle the order split and external quote paths, invoice lines with an accrual hook, plus new server-side quote functions for the wizard covering hosting and email orders that return cart-price-shaped results, replacing the matching logic in order.tsx.

I'm switching order.tsx to async quotes using the existing sequence/debounce pattern, keeping catalog fields around for per-plan display cards while removing matrix-based totals. Hosting quotes need an ipHash from request headers for eligibility checks, and the renewal totals subtract the recurring partner discount from the full charge for both hosting and email — I should also verify the auth-lockouts test suite doesn't break against the new server action files.

For renewals, I'm working out how the hosting and email due-sweeps should compute discounted pricing per account using the partner discount, updating invoice line items to include a negative partner discount line, and making sure upcoming-balance warnings and top-up calculations use the discounted price too so they don't misfire. I'm considering whether to reuse the existing renewalCharge helper (already used for VPS/game) for hosting and email as well, rather than writing separate discount logic.

Next I'm adding coupon support for game deploys by wiring a hidden coupon field into the game branch of the deploy form, and confirming the PayPal order creation already reads that coupon from form data correctly. Then I'm turning to whether hosting and email should support coupons at all — since the server currently has no coupon logic for those products, I need to check whether admins can even create a HOSTING-scoped coupon, and if so, whether silently ignoring it during hosting checkout is the same class of bug, which means I should surface an explicit error like "Promo codes aren't available for Web Hosting yet" instead of failing silently.

content.content:
## Creator Partner Program — agency/KOL commission + a real customer discount

**What it does.** An agency or content creator gets a permanent link. Every customer who signs up
through it is attached to that partner FOR LIFE (one partner per customer, enforced by a DB unique
constraint) and gets a real, sitewide discount for as long as they stay a customer — **50% off their
first purchase of any service except a domain, then 10% off every purchase after that, forever**
(new orders AND renewals). The partner earns a **lifetime commission** (their own negotiated
`commissionRatePct`, default 20%) on every qualifying charge that customer ever makes, with one
carve-out: a dedicated-IP add-on line earns the partner 0% (everything else on the same
order/renewal still earns the full rate).

This is a DIFFERENT program from "Refer & earn" (`User.referralCode`, the row above this one) — a
peer-to-peer, one-time wallet bonus. A single `?ref=`/`nxeon_ref` cookie can only ever mean ONE of
the two: at registration (`lib/actions.ts` `register()`), an ACTIVE `ReferralPartner.code` match
always wins over a `User.referralCode` match, so nobody double-dips a partner commission AND a peer
referral bonus off the same signup.

**Data model** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ReferralPartner` | The partner: `code` (unique, uppercase), `commissionRatePct` (per-partner, frozen onto each commission row at accrual), `status` (ACTIVE/PAUSED — pausing stops BOTH new commission AND the customer discount), optional `userId` login |
| `PartnerCustomer` | The lifetime attachment. `customerId` UNIQUE — one partner per customer, ever. `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` (null until their first discounted purchase; null = 50% tier, set = 10% tier forever) |
| `PartnerCommission` | One row per qualifying PAID invoice, `invoiceId` UNIQUE (idempotent). `baseCents` = net charge minus that invoice's `dedicatedIpCents` — the dedicated-IP exclusion |
| `PartnerPayout` | A REAL payment made to the partner off-wallet (bank/Wise/PayPal), can be partial. Balance = `sum(PartnerCommission, status != VOID) − sum(PartnerPayout)` — NOT derived from commission-row status alone (see the model's own doc comment for why a partial payout needs a separate ledger) |
| `PartnerInvite` | Two kinds (`kind`). `LOGIN`: a pending invite for a brand-new (non-customer) login on an admin-made partner — token-hash/expiry, mirrors `OrgInvite`'s mechanics. `CREATOR` (2026-09-27): an invite made BEFORE any partner exists — `partnerId` is null until claimed; carries `name`, `note`, `ratePct`, `allowAnyEmail`, the CSV prefill (`channelUrl`, `primaryGame`, `country`, `subscribers`), `lastSentAt` (NULL = DRAFT, never emailed) and `sendCount` |
| `PartnerPayoutProfile` (2026-09-27) | One per partner: the partner's own contact fields (plain) + preferred payout method; the method-specific details and note are sealed in `payoutDetailsEnc` with `lib/crypto-box.ts` (AES-256-GCM from `AUTH_SECRET`). `payoutUpdatedAt` shown to admins |
| `ReferralClick` (existing, previously unused) | One row per real link click — `code`, `ipHash`, `referer`, `convertedUserId` (best-effort, set at registration to the most recent unconverted click for that code) |
| `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` | How much of that invoice's net amount is the dedicated-IP surcharge — a real typed column, populated by every charge path that can bill one (`lib/order.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`), never inferred by parsing line items after the fact |

**The links.** `nxeon.cloud/partner/<code>` (`app/partner/[code]/route.ts`) is the REAL link partners
are given — it records a `ReferralClick` row, then sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie and 302s to
`/register`, exactly like the older `/r/<code>` (peer-referral short link), which now ALSO records a
click (same table — its own schema comment always said it covers both code namespaces).

**Automatic attachment.** `register()` (`lib/actions.ts`) reads `nxeon_ref`; if it matches an ACTIVE
partner code, `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` (`lib/partner-commission.ts`) creates the
`PartnerCustomer` row right there — no admin action needed for the normal case. `adminAttachCustomer`
(`lib/actions-partner.ts`) remains for support/edge cases (attaching an existing account by email).

  meaning (the creator path answers "not a creator code"). New self-chosen codes are already
  collision-checked against coupons at claim; admin-made ones weren't. Stacking is unchanged: one
  code in the box at a time; after a creator code is applied the box is free for a coupon, and — as
  already for link-attributed customers — the partner discount is applied AFTER intro + coupon on
  what's left (`lib/order.ts` / `lib/game-order.ts` `preDiscountChargeCents`), with the coupon's own
  rules (`firstTimeOnly`, caps…) untouched.
- **Product scope** is the existing discount's: VPS and game servers. On hosting / email / domains
  the code still links the account (the discount then applies to their first server order) and the
  wizard says so ("The creator discount applies to VPS and game server orders").
- Google/Discord sign-up never attributed a partner (neither reads `nxeon_ref`); those accounts can
  now use the checkout box before their first purchase.

**The customer discount** — pure math in `lib/partner-discount.ts` (`PARTNER_FIRST_PURCHASE_PCT` =
50, `PARTNER_RECURRING_PCT` = 10), DB resolution in `lib/partner-pricing.ts`
(`partnerDiscountForNewOrder`, `partnerDiscountForRenewal`, `partnerPreviewForCode`/`ForUser` for
pre-purchase marketing messaging). Wired into:
- `lib/order.ts` `orderQuote`/`placeOrder` (VPS) and `lib/game-order.ts` `gameOrderQuote`/

# Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)

Seven commits, newest first. This document was last verified at `4ea9790`; everything above it in this
table is what the current pass folded in.

| Commit | Subject | Verified state |
|---|---|---|
| `2d8fedd` | Game servers renew at their game-plan price, not the base VPS plan | **Real.** `renewalQuote` delegates to `renewalCharge` and owns no arithmetic; a test asserts the file contains none. The extraction of `lib/renewal-charge.ts` was forced by a bundling failure (`Can't resolve 'fs'`) that `tsc` could not see |
| `f28f15e` | Refuse truncated Stripe metadata; one quote per order; honest receipt | **Real.** `packMetadata` throws before `checkout.sessions.create`; the sold price rides in metadata; the receipt attaches an invoice or points at billing history, never promises one it does not send |
| `3aa24d7` | Verification gates, auth lockouts, email verification (gate ships OFF) | **Mixed by design.** The two auth lockouts and the NAT flush are genuinely fixed. Email verification is **complete and deliberately disarmed** — `email_verification_enforced` defaults to `false` because the platform's DKIM record is missing (gaps 1 and 9). Two of the three agents behind this commit were killed mid-task; what is recorded here is what was verified afterwards, not what was intended |
| `7490131` | Stop charging customers without consent; card-save UI | **Real.** Three launch blockers from `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, all reproduced in a browser and all byte-identical in production, plus the card-save UI that had been wrongly marked complete |
| `156b6ac` | Harden the post-cutover TLS sweep against its own first live run | **Real, and verified on the live queue** rather than asserted: jobs drain, the permanent path settles, notifications stopped climbing |
| `4ea9790` | Promo-basis proration, post-cutover TLS, 8 more migration defects | **Real.** `Server.termPromoPercent` makes the proration round trip net zero by construction; the TLS pass stopped being dead code; 4 rows backfilled from real billing records with 0 fallbacks |
| `fd71056` | Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI | **Real.** Nine engine defects, the `capMonths` asymmetry, the sub-Stripe-floor card leg, and the first CI workflow |

The through-line across all seven is the defect this codebase keeps producing in new places: **a second
definition of something that already had one.** A second renewal formula. A second promo basis. A
second place `lastAutoBackup` could be written. A second email-normalisation. The fix, every time, was
to delete the duplicate rather than to make the two agree.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker

input.message:
Both bugs are fixed on `fix/partner-discount-all-checkouts`. It's one commit, `af0d5f9a58`, on top of `52fa0563b3`, pushed to origin and deployed to staging (`deploy-staging.sh` exit 0, HTTP 200, no errors in the staging web/worker logs). On staging, the quote now matches the Stripe amount for VPS, game, hosting and email. What is still unverified is the paid step itself: I never paid, so nothing has run the code that charges the wallet, writes the invoice or bills a renewal (listed at the end).

## What changed per product

**Web hosting and business email (bug 1)**
- **One price function each:** `hostingOrderDueCents` in `lib/hosting-pricing.ts` and `emailOrderDueCents` in `lib/email-pricing.ts`. They use the existing `partnerDiscountForNewOrder`, which applies the same "first purchase" test order.ts uses (`firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` is null).
- **Every step uses that function:**
  - the wizard quote;
  - the wallet/card split in `placeHostingOrder` and `orderEmailHosting`;
  - the PayPal/Coinbase quotes in `lib/actions-payment-providers.ts`;
  - the charge in `orderHostingAccountFor` and `orderEmailHostingCore`.
- **Inside the charge transaction** the discount is applied last, after first-month-free, and covers plan plus storage. The 50% first-purchase slot is claimed there with `claimPartnerFirstPurchase`, the same lost-race handling as order.ts. The invoice gets a base line plus a negative line with the same wording VPS and game use.
- **Judgment call — a $0 order doesn't use up the 50%.** A monthly hosting order with first-month-free costs $0, so it gets no discount and doesn't consume the 50% slot. The new `applyPartnerDiscount` in `lib/partner-discount.ts` returns tier `NONE` in that case. This matches commission (which skips $0 invoices) and the creator-code "paid purchase" test. If you'd rather the free month count as the first purchase, it's a one-line change.
- **Wizard quote is now server-side:** `components/nx/order.tsx` used to read hosting/email prices from a per-plan table built into the page, which can't know about the customer's partner link. New files `lib/nx/quote-hosting.ts` and `lib/nx/quote-email.ts` each have one export that calls `requireUser`. Side effect: on annual hosting terms the first-month-free credit shown now equals what's actually charged; the old table used the plan's full monthly price.
- **Coupons:** coupons only exist for VPS and game (`CouponServiceKind` is ANY/VPS/GAME). A code typed on a hosting or email order now shows "Promo codes apply to Cloud VPS and Game Server orders only." instead of being silently ignored.
- **Renewals:** hosting and email renewals did not get the 10%. They do now, in `worker/product-renewals.ts`: `partnerDiscountForRenewal` is applied, with its own negative invoice line, and the email "renews soon" warning uses the discounted amount.
- **Commission:** it already accrued on hosting and email invoices through the background reconcile sweep, since every PAID invoice qualifies. I added the same immediate accrual call VPS and game already make; commission rules are unchanged.
- **Copy:** the wizard's creator-code panel and `/register` said "first server order" and "applies to VPS and game server orders". They now say "first order", with domains excluded.

**Game coupon (bug 2)**
- `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`: the game payment form now includes the hidden `couponCode` field, same as VPS (creator codes excluded). The server re-checks the coupon exactly as before; redemption rules are untouched.
- Extra fix, in `lib/nx/quote.ts` and `lib/nx/quote-game.ts`: when the account isn't eligible for a coupon, the preview used to add the coupon back onto the total. That left the partner discount calculated on the wrong base, so the quote was off from the charge. It now re-prices without the coupon, the way the card path already did.

## Verification
- **Typecheck:** `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean, with no errors of any kind.
- **Tests:**
  - 6 new tests in `test/partner-discount.test.ts`, all passing.
  - `test/payment-providers.test.ts` checks the price functions by name, so I updated it to the new function names.
  - Full suite: 38 failures, identical to the base branch apart from that one updated test. They include 3 in `auth-lockouts`; the new quote files are not flagged by its guard check.
- **Staging** (two new @example.com accounts; A came in through `/partner/ADVIDEO`, B through the checkout code box). Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/checkout-fixes/`.

| Product | Account | Quote shows | Stripe test session amount | Screenshot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VPS | A | 50% line | 649 (= quote) | `vps-quote.png` |
| Hosting, annual | A | first-month-free + 50% line | 1315 (= quote) | `hosting-annual-quote.png` |
| Hosting, monthly | A | $0, no partner line (by design) | — | `hosting-monthly-freemonth.png` |
| Email | A | 50% line | 99 (= quote) | `email-quote.png` |
| Game (Rust) | B | 50% line after "Apply creator code"; STAY50 then shows "50% off" too | 1299 → 649 → 324 | `game-0` … `game-3` |

- **The game coupon reached the server:**
  - 3 of the recorded order requests carried STAY50;
  - a `CouponRedemption` row (STAY50, 650, RESERVED) exists for account B;
  - the 324 session carries the matching reservation token.

## Unverified
- The paid step itself, for every product: charging the wallet, the invoice lines, claiming the first-purchase slot, and commission accrual. I never paid, so this is covered only by code review and typecheck.
- Hosting and email renewals with the partner discount; no renewal ran on staging.
- The PayPal/Coinbase paths for hosting and email (PayPal is not enabled on staging).

## Notes
- The page left on staging:
  - several Stripe test-mode sessions;
  - one STAY50 hold that expires at 03:08 today;
  - two test accounts linked to ADVIDEO.
- Known, not changed:
  - Card payments for hosting and email are re-priced when the payment completes. If the customer's own other "first" order uses the 50% slot in between, the charge can fail with "Insufficient balance" after the card has cleared. The money stays in their wallet as credit. This is the same risk first-month-free already has.
  - Plan upgrades (VPS and hosting) and the renewal amounts shown on "My Services" don't include the partner discount for any product.
  - The hosting/email line in the order summary shows "—" for its price. That was already the case.
- Docs: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` has a dated change-history entry, plus updates to the Creator Partner Program section and the product-renewals paragraph. There was no ROADMAP item to tick.

content.thinking:
So an unexpired own reserved hold blocks a new reserve, causing the coupon to be silently dropped at charge time while the wizard still shows the discount — the quote logic only checks eligibility errors like first-time-only or exclusions, not existing holds, so the displayed price wrongly includes the coupon. I'm now looking at how the prepared session in the wizard is keyed.

Since it's keyed on cardDue, any change to that value (toggling a coupon, entering a creator code) reruns prepare and creates a new reserve, which can collide with a hold from an earlier prepare in the same session — for example applying STAY50 first, then a creator code, causes the second reserve attempt to be refused because the first hold is still active, leaving the session at a coupon-less price while the UI still displays the discount. This is a genuine single-checkout bug, and I'm considering fixing it in reserveOrderCoupon by releasing the user's own still-live RESERVED holds for the same coupon before reserving again, though I need to weigh the risk that an old Stripe session tied to that hold might still get paid if the customer has two tabs open.

Releasing that hold prematurely could let someone exploit the same coupon twice — once through the old session's fulfilment (which would fail to find its hold but still "keep" the discounted price without a redemption row) and once through the new session. Since the hold row doesn't store which Stripe session created it, I can't easily expire the old session to close this gap, so I'm leaning toward a safer approach: if the user already has a live RESERVED hold for the coupon, just reuse and return that same token instead of creating a new one.

Silently falling back to full price without telling the UI seems like the real gap — the checkout total updates but the display doesn't, which is misleading either way. Returning an outright error blocks a customer from ever using their coupon while their own hold is active, which feels too harsh. The better path is probably reusing the customer's own hold via the token, but then I need to close the loophole where a second concurrent paid session with that same token still slips through and keeps the discounted price after the first one consumes it.

Practically this is a narrow edge case: it needs two parallel checkouts in the same ~70-minute window, both fully paid, and the redemption cap still only increments once — so the actual damage is just one extra discount, which feels tolerable. Still, I should flag this to the coordinator rather than quietly deciding, since their instruction was that coupon redemption rules stay untouched, and this fix technically alters reservation behavior even if it doesn't change the per-person redemption limit itself.

I also consider whether releasing and expiring the old Stripe session is feasible, but Stripe's Checkout Sessions API doesn't support metadata-based search, so that route is out. And I check the IP uniqueness constraint — since the reuse lookup is scoped to userId, a hold from a different user on the same IP would still correctly hit the unique constraint and get refused.

Now I'm sketching the actual reservation reuse logic inside reserveOrderCoupon: after releasing expired holds, I look up an existing reserved redemption for this coupon and user that hasn't expired yet, and if found, update its amount and expiry and return its existing reservation token instead of creating a new one. This needs to sit after the firstTimeOnly/exclusion checks but before the cap increment, since that slot is already counted. I still need to verify how releaseExpiredCouponHoldsFor checks reservedUntil against now, and think through how the checkout.session.expired webhook should release the old session's hold.

But now I realize there's a real bug: when the old Stripe session expires, the webhook releases the hold by token, and since that token is now shared with the new session, it releases the new session's hold too. Then when the new session tries to fulfill, confirmation fails silently, the discount stays applied, and timesRedeemed gets decremented — leaking a cap slot. Staging doesn't run the webhook, but production does, and old sessions typically expire before new ones since they were created earlier, so this collision is very plausible. I need to figure out a mitigation, maybe generating a new token on reuse instead of reusing the same one.

There's a related bug: if the customer switches to wallet payment after already having a card-session hold, claimOrderCoupon would try to claim again and hit the same P2002 "already used" error. I should check claimOrderCoupon to see if it can similarly convert an existing live hold into a CONSUMED state instead of failing.

input.message:
The paid step is verified for hosting and email, and the partner tiers (50% first, 10% after) work end to end. The paid game order hit a real bug, and a VPS termination hit a second one. Both are fixed on the branch, but I could not re-verify them or run the renewal test: another session has redeployed staging with its own branch and still has it there. Still unverified: the game fix, the refund fix, and hosting/email renewals.

## Paid orders on staging (Stripe test card 4242, card path in the deploy wizard)
Amounts are USD cents; the wizard showed SGD at about 1.34. I used the card path inside the order flow because the staging top-up UI isn't exposed. Each order shows up as a card credit to the wallet followed by a debit of the same amount.

| Product | Quoted | Debited | Invoice lines | First-purchase slot | Commission (ADVIDEO, 40%) | Coupon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Hosting, annual, account A (first purchase) | 1315 (S$17.62) | 1315 | 2631 base, −1316 "Partner discount — 50% off your first purchase" | claimed | 526 on 1315, ACCRUED | n/a |
| 2. Email, new account C via /partner/ADVIDEO | 99 (S$1.33) | 99 | 199 base, −100 50% line | claimed | 40 on 99, ACCRUED | n/a |
| 3. Game (Rust), account B, creator code + STAY50 | **324 (S$4.34)** | **649** | 1299 base, −650 50% line (no coupon line) | claimed | 260 on 649, ACCRUED | **Not applied.** B's STAY50 row stayed RESERVED; it was a hold from my earlier unpaid visit |
| 4. Second order by A (VPS; hosting/email were not on staging any more) | 1169 (S$15.66) | 1169 | 1299 base, −130 "Partner discount — 10% off" | already used, so 10% applied | 468 on 1169, ACCRUED | n/a |

## Bug 1 (game): the charge dropped the coupon while the wizard still showed it
Fixed in commit `06ec2f45f0`.
- **What happens:** every time the wizard prepares a card session, it reserves the coupon. That happens again if the amount changes, or if the customer comes back to checkout within the ~70 minutes a coupon hold lasts. `reserveOrderCoupon` refused the new reservation because the customer's own earlier hold already occupied the one-per-person slot.
- **Why the customer overpays:** every card and PayPal caller then silently re-priced the Stripe session without the coupon. The wizard still showed the discount, and its button still read "Pay S$4.34" while Stripe charged S$8.70.
- **Fix, in `lib/coupon-redemption.ts`:**
  - An account's own live hold is now moved to the new checkout: same row and already-counted cap slot, with a new token.
  - The wizard preview now also checks the existing "already used" rule, per account and per IP, so a repeat customer isn't shown a discount the charge will refuse. The redemption rules themselves are unchanged.
- **Trade-off for you:** if a customer pays two open checkout sessions, the older one keeps its discounted price with no hold behind it. That is the existing documented fallback, and it never overcharges.
- **Still possible:** losing a race for a coupon's last redemption slot between quote and payment still re-prices without telling the wizard. That behaviour predates this branch and is rare.

## Bug 2 (VPS): immediate termination refunded more than the customer paid
Fixed in commit `7ad59ebc0f`.
- **What happened:** when I terminated A's VPS, the customer paid 1169 and was refunded 1280. At the 50% tier, buying and immediately terminating would return roughly double the payment.
- **Cause:** `refundableTermCents` in `lib/order.ts` ignored the partner discount.
- **Fix:** it now subtracts the plan's share of that discount. Rows already created keep their old refund amount.
- Games get no prorated refund, and neither do hosting or email.

## Blocked
- **Staging is taken:** at 02:19 another session deployed `fix/vps-ram-allocation` over my build, and it is still there. I tried to deploy a combined branch of both fixes; the permission check denied it as modifying a shared resource. I aborted that and deleted the local branch, and did not deploy over their work.
- **Still to run once staging is free:**
  - redeploy `fix/partner-discount-all-checkouts` (head `7ad59ebc0f`);
  - re-run the game order with STAY50 for a fresh account and for a returning one;
  - confirm STAY50 moves from RESERVED to CONSUMED;

## Bug 1 (game): the charge dropped the coupon while the wizard still showed it

That happens again if the amount changes, or if the customer comes back to checkout within the ~70 minutes a coupon hold lasts. `reserveOrderCoupon` refused the new reservation because the customer's own earlier hold already occupied the one-per-person slot.
- **Why the customer overpays:** every card and PayPal caller then silently re-priced the Stripe session without the coupon. The wizard still showed the discount, and its button still read "Pay S$4.34" while Stripe charged S$8.70.
- **Fix, in `lib/coupon-redemption.ts`:**

- **Trade-off for you:** if a customer pays two open checkout sessions, the older one keeps its discounted price with no hold behind it. That is the existing documented fallback, and it never overcharges.

content.thinking:
The total charged of 324 matches, but the line-item split is off: the partner discount line shows 650 instead of the correct 325, while the base line absorbs the difference at 974. I trace this to placeGameOrder pulling partnerDiscountCents directly from the quote rather than recalculating it against the consumed coupon state.

- A trial coupon on a card-paid game order probably gives a full month instead of the trial days. Fulfilment re-prices without the coupon, so `couponTrialDays` would be lost. This predates this branch and I did not check it.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Game order with STAY50, customer returning to checkout | **Pass.** Quoted $3.24, charged $3.24. STAY50 moved from reserved to used (one row). 50% first-purchase discount applied; 40% commission accrued. |
| Game invoice lines after a card-paid coupon order | **Was wrong, now fixed and re-verified.** The total was right but the lines split the discount wrongly: $9.74 base / −$6.50 partner instead of $6.49 / −$3.25. A new order with a different coupon (TRIAL798) now shows correct lines: $2.98 base / −$1.49 partner. |
| Game order with STAY50 from a second new account | **Not re-run.** All test traffic comes from one IP and STAY50 allows one use per IP. That account was correctly told "You've already used this code." and charged what the quote showed. |
| VPS termination refund | **Pass.** Paid $11.69 (10% off), refunded $11.52, so the refund is below what was paid. |
| Email renewal | **Pass.** $1.99 base, −$0.20 partner line (10%), $1.79 debited, commission accrued. |
| Hosting renewal | **Pass.** $28.70 base, −$2.87 partner line, $25.83 debited, commission accrued. |
| Merge into `release/nxm-launch` + clean staging deploy | **Not done, blocked.** |

- A customer's own earlier coupon reservation made a new checkout drop the coupon at payment while the screen still showed it. Their reservation now carries over to the new checkout.
- VPS termination refunds ignored the partner discount, so they paid back more than the customer paid.
- After a coupon changed the total, the card form stayed attached to the first Stripe session and charged the pre-coupon amount.
- Game invoices showed the wrong split between the base price and the partner discount.
- The checkout preview now tells a customer "already used" before payment, instead of showing a discount the charge would refuse.

All test servers were terminated through the portal. On staging I did two things with your authorisation: pushed two test subscriptions' renewal dates into the past, and topped up two test accounts with $50 each through the real Add funds flow.

Two older issues I noticed but left alone, per your stop instruction:
- A trial coupon on a card-paid game order probably gives a full month instead of the trial days. This is unverified.
- Commission stays accrued on orders that are later terminated and refunded.

**Decision needed:** to finish, `fix/partner-discount-all-checkouts` needs merging into `release/nxm-launch` in `/root/nxeon-worktrees/release`. It's a clean merge from `52fa0563b3`.
